sections.heading: Water Damage Risk Through the Frisco Seasons

items.title: Spring
items.text: Spring brings North Texas's heaviest thunderstorm activity, increasing the risk of flash flooding and roof leaks across Frisco neighborhoods.

items.title: Summer
items.text: Summer heat can stress plumbing systems and irrigation lines, while sudden severe storms can still bring heavy rainfall and localized flooding.

items.title: Fall
items.text: Fall weather in Frisco can shift quickly, with occasional heavy rain events that test aging gutters, roofing, and drainage systems.

items.title: Winter
items.text: Winter in Frisco occasionally brings freezing temperatures that can cause pipes to freeze and burst, leading to sudden indoor water damage.

sections.heading: Water Damage Restoration FAQs for Frisco Homeowners

items.q: How quickly should I act after discovering water damage in my Frisco home?
items.a: Acting as soon as possible is important — the longer water sits, the greater the risk to flooring, walls, and belongings. Contact us right away so we can assess the situation and begin restoration.

items.q: Will my homeowner's insurance cover water damage restoration?
items.a: Coverage depends on your specific policy and the cause of the damage. We provide detailed documentation of the damage and restoration work to support your claim, but we recommend confirming coverage details directly with your insurance provider.

items.q: Is it safe for me to remove standing water myself?
items.a: Standing water can carry hidden electrical or contamination hazards, so we recommend avoiding direct contact and contacting a professional team to assess and safely extract the water.
